description: FIRST REVOLVE GOLDEN (new curved-topology class — a solid of revolution): a rectangular profile offset from the axis, revolved 360 deg into an annular cylinder (a washer). A two-feature TREE (sketch -> revolve) evaluated through the same evaluate-tree path as the extrude/fillet goldens: planegcs solve -> profile wire assembly + closed-wire check (SHARED build_profile_face — construction geometry excluded) -> face -> revolution about a sketch-line axis (a construction centerline, resolved to world via the SHARED plane->world mapping) -> add against the (empty) body -> GProp on the evaluated body -> tessellation -> content-addressed GLB. Locks: the revolve handler + axis resolution + axis-clears-profile guard, GProp over two coaxial cylindrical surfaces + two annular caps, curved-face tessellation of the periodic (seamed) cylinders, and (via the parametrized round-trip gate) STEP re-approximation of the revolved cylindrical surfaces.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). The profile is a rectangle r in [r_i=10, r_o=20] mm, height y in [0, h=15] mm, drawn on the XY datum plane; the axis is a CONSTRUCTION line along sketch x=0 (the sketch Y axis). Revolving 360 deg about it sweeps the rectangle into an annular cylinder coaxial with the world Y axis (sketch-Y maps to world Y on the XY plane).

The sketch is constrained at its analytic solution with zero residual (4 corner coincidences, horizontal e1, vertical e2, vertical axis, distance e1=10, distance e2=15). It is underconstrained (the profile's position DOF remain), so planegcs provably returns the input positions bitwise — verified 2026-07-11 (solved == input; same solver posture as the extrude/fillet goldens). The construction axis is excluded from the profile but present for the revolve to reference.
volume = pi*(r_o^2 - r_i^2)*h = pi*(400 - 100)*15 = 4500*pi = 14137.16694115407 mm^3 (annulus cross-section area pi*(r_o^2-r_i^2) swept the full turn).

surface_area outer cylinder lateral = 2*pi*r_o*h = 2*pi*20*15 = 600*pi; inner cylinder lateral = 2*pi*r_i*h = 2*pi*10*15 = 300*pi; two annular caps = 2 * pi*(r_o^2-r_i^2) = 2*300*pi = 600*pi. Total = 600*pi + 300*pi + 600*pi = 1500*pi = 4712.38898038469 mm^2.

centroid = (0, 7.5, 0) mm: the body is symmetric about the world Y axis (the axis of revolution, through the origin at x=z=0) and about the y=h/2 plane, so the centroid sits on the axis at mid-height. (GProp puts x,z at ulp scale ~2e-15, y exactly 7.5.)
bounding_box = [-20,0,-20]..[20,15,20]: outer radius r_o=20 about the world Y axis gives x,z in [-20,20]; the height spans y in [0,15]; the inner hole does not affect the AABB.

topology: 4 faces (outer cylinder, inner cylinder, top annular cap, bottom annular cap), 6 edges (1 seam line on each of the two periodic cylinders + outer & inner boundary circles on each of the two caps = 1 + 1 + 2 + 2), 1 shell. Vertices = 4 (the two endpoints of each cylinder's seam edge). The naive polyhedral Euler check does NOT apply here: the cylinder faces are periodic (one seam) and each cap is a single face bounded by TWO loops (outer + inner circle), so V-E+F = 4-6+4 = 2 is a B-rep count, not a genus statement — a washer solid is a solid torus (genus 1).

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad, isRelative=False): each full circle discretizes to 2*ceil(2*pi/0.1) = 126 segments — the same 2x-angular-estimate rule the cylinder golden exhibits. Outer cylinder = 127x2 node grid (seam node duplicated) = 254 nodes, 126*2 = 252 triangles. Inner cylinder = 126x2 nodes = 252 nodes, 252 triangles. Each annular cap triangulates as a strip between its outer 126-gon and inner 126-gon = 252 boundary nodes, 2*126 = 252 triangles, no interior node. Two caps -> 504 nodes / 504 triangles.

mesh totals = 254 + 252 + 252 + 254 = 1012 vertices and 252 + 252 + 252 + 252 = 1008 triangles (per-face faceted normals, no vertex sharing across faces — same convention as the box, cylinder, and fillet goldens).

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: CURVED-GEOMETRY tolerance, measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). The two coaxial cylindrical surfaces go through OCCT's Gauss-quadrature surface/volume integration in GProp — converging to machine precision but not exact zero. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-11, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume 1.82e-12 mm^3 (~1.3e-16 relative, one-ulp scale at 1.4e4), surface_area exactly 0.0, centroid <= 2.06e-15 mm (x/z on the axis; y exactly 7.5), AABB exactly 0.0 on all six bounds. Documented ceiling 1e-9 = ~5.5e5x the observed worst case, headroom for libm/platform variation in the quadrature's transcendental evaluations across CI hosts — while staying 100x TIGHTER than the standing planar 1e-7 bound, matching the cylinder/extrude/fillet goldens' posture. The solver contributes zero error by construction (zero-residual start, solved == input bitwise). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
